annotations.annotation_text: Cabalistic number 1132 on page 310 ("The Tavern"): Joyce encodes mystical and historical intervals throughout the Wake. Within HCE behind the bar at his Chapelizod pub, the Norwegian Captain tale, the television broadcast, the twelve customers drinking and judging, this number resonates with Dublin dates, Viconian divisions, and the mathematical architecture underlying the dream's Age of Heroes phase.
sources: Hart, Clive. Structure and Motif in Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/structuremotifin0000hart
McHugh, Roland. Annotations to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/annotationstofin0000mchu_h5g8

annotations.annotation_text: Oneiric dimension "night" on page 310 ("The Tavern"): the nocturnal consciousness surfaces within HCE behind the bar at his Chapelizod pub, the Norwegian Captain tale, the television broadcast, the twelve customers drinking and judging. During this Age of Heroes phase, Joyce reconstructs the sleeping body's sensory deprivation — dimmed sight, distorted hearing, dream-logic association — transforming somatic experience into polyphonic language.
sources: Bishop, John. Joyce's Book of the Dark. https://archive.org/details/joycesbookofdark0000bish
Freud, Sigmund. The Interpretation of Dreams. https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/4349
Troy, Mark L. Mummeries of Resurrection. http://www.rosenlake.net
